paper.title: Drift Plus Optimistic Penalty: A Learning Framework for Stochastic Network Optimization with Improved Regret Bounds

settings.name_in_paper: Joint routing and scheduling in multi-commodity queueing networks with unknown edge transmission costs
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Stochastic network control with queue dynamics: queue backlogs (and terminal backlog cost) depend on past routing/scheduling actions, i.e. a state-dependent (MDP-like) control problem rather than an i.i.d. bandit; cost learning part is a stochastic semi-bandit.
unmapped: Multi-hop queueing network with stochastic bounded arrivals at unknown rates strictly inside the stability region (epsilon-interior)
Actions are per-edge per-commodity transmission rates in a capacity polytope; cost linear in planned transmissions with unknown edge costs c_ij in [0, C_max]
Total cost includes a terminal backlog cost C_B per undelivered packet at time T
Noisy cost observed for each edge with positive planned transmission (semi-bandit on edges)
Learner does not know arrival rates or costs; observes queue backlogs
settings.definition_quote: We consider a multi-hop network $G = (\mc{N},\mc{E})$ ... At each $t$, the policy receives a \emph{noisy observation} $ \widetilde{c}_{ij} (t)$ for each edge on which it transmitted any packets ... $\eta_{ij}(t)$'s are zero mean $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian ... $R^\pi(T) := \Ex [C^\pi(T)] - \inf_{\pi^*\in\Pi^*} \Ex[ C^{\pi^*}(T)]$.

symbols.C_B: terminal backlog cost per undelivered packet
symbols.C_L: finite constant depending on topology and costs (Theorem 1)

conditions: arrival rates strictly inside the stability region (epsilon > 0 slack)

source.label: thm:regret_theorem
source.quote: \emph{(DPOP Regret)} For $C_B \geq C_L$, the DPOP policy $\pi_D$ achieves a sub-linear regret of $R^{\pi_D}(T) = O\left(\sqrt{T}\log T\right)$ with parameters $\beta > 4\sigma^2$, $\delta = T^{-{2\sigma^2}/{\beta}}$, and $\nu = \sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: Regret = E[C^pi(T)] - inf over all policies (with knowledge of costs and future arrivals) of E[C^{pi*}(T)]; recorded as pseudo_regret vs best_policy. Constants depend on network size, capacities, C_max, C_B, epsilon. The proof combines Propositions 1-4: R1 = O(sqrt(T) log T), R2 = O(1), R3 = O(sqrt(T)) and R4 = O(sqrt(T log T)). The text also says nu = O(sqrt(T/max(C_B,1))) gives O(min(sqrt(C_B), C_B) sqrt(T) log T). Parameters depend on T, so the horizon is known.
